title: Protonation state as a routine crystallographic observable

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a routine crystallographic method for determining where labile hydrogen atoms are, which chemical sites carry protons, and how those assignments are distributed across a crystal. Its principal target is ordinary-sized macromolecular and catalytic crystals at practical measurement times and radiation doses. Rather than assigning protonation mainly from chemical expectations, researchers would obtain experimentally constrained hydrogen coordinates, site occupancies and protonation states, with uncertainties and unresolved alternatives reported explicitly.

Concept synthesis: locating a hydrogen, determining its occupancy and assigning a site's protonation state are related but distinct tasks. A convincing method must distinguish a well-localized hydrogen from a partially occupied or disordered site and avoid turning an ambiguous measurement into a categorical chemical assignment. The intended advance extends beyond selected, well-ordered organic microcrystals to chemically varied macromolecular and catalytic samples. Extension to functional materials is an additional ambition requiring its own validation.

significance.text: Conditional significance: routine access to protonation and hydrogen geometry would add chemically decisive information to structures used to study acid–base reactions, catalytic intermediates and metal coordination. It would help distinguish alternative interpretations of otherwise similar heavy-atom arrangements and make protonation assignments more directly testable. Pharmaceutical salt-versus-cocrystal identification is a narrower example of the chemical distinctions that hydrogen-sensitive measurements can support; the supplied research attributes such assignments in three pharmaceuticals to electron diffraction.

Conditional downstream impact: reliable measurements across different chemical conditions could strengthen studies of enzyme mechanisms, proton-coupled electron transfer and proton-conducting materials by constraining the positions and populations of relevant chemical states. A static hydrogen arrangement would not, by itself, establish a reaction mechanism, the order of proton transfers or a functioning transport pathway. Those conclusions can require kinetics, dynamics and complementary measurements under the conditions in which the chemistry occurs.

Interpretive limit: the aspiration to make hydrogen assignments as dependable as routine carbon positions describes a desired level of usability, not an established equivalence. Disordered or partially occupied hydrogen sites may remain intrinsically ambiguous, and useful reliability must include calibrated uncertainty and the ability to leave a site unresolved. The revolutionary change would be broad, dependable access to chemically informative measurements, rather than a promise that every proton becomes uniquely visible.

missing_breakthrough.text: The missing capability is a broadly applicable, dose-tolerant measurement and refinement method that recovers labile hydrogen information from ordinary macromolecular and catalytic crystals at useful throughput. The supplied research identifies complementary limitations in existing approaches: X-rays probe electron density, making hydrogen particularly difficult when its electron density is strongly polarized and making a bare proton a particularly poor direct target; neutron measurements offer nuclear sensitivity but impose substantial sample and instrument demands. These are the motivating physical distinctions in the supplied account, whose cited source texts were not retained for verification.

For electron diffraction, the supplied research identifies hydrogen sensitivity as a promising route while naming multiple scattering, radiation damage and disorder as obstacles to general hydrogen refinement. The engineering challenge is to extract defensible hydrogen information despite these effects and to demonstrate that favorable small-organic results extend to chemically complex samples. Reported refinement of selected ordered compounds is an important lead, but it does not establish reliable recovery of labile, disordered or partially occupied hydrogen sites in macromolecules.

Engineering synthesis: success requires both adequate measurement sensitivity and an inference procedure that distinguishes information supplied by the experiment from information imposed by chemical constraints or a refinement model. The method must quantify positional and occupancy uncertainty, identify competing protonation assignments, detect dose-dependent changes and report failures. It must also retain practical sample-size, collection-time and instrument-access requirements across a representative range of samples.

current_state.text: The supplied research attributes to a Crystal Growth & Design paper, reported as published online on 17 December 2024 with DOI 10.1021/acs.cgd.4c01421, electron-diffraction identification of hydrogens sufficient to distinguish salts from cocrystals in three pharmaceuticals. This describes a specific small-molecule application. It does not establish routine protonation determination across proteins, catalytic crystals or functional materials. The attribution comes from the supplied abstract-level account; no retained source text was available to the review to confirm the examples, methods or scope.

A second reported result concerns Hirshfeld atom refinement of electron-diffraction data. The supplied research attributes to Yörük, Brázda and Palatinus, in a Journal of Molecular Structure article dated 25 October 2025 with DOI 10.1016/j.molstruc.2025.142798, free hydrogen refinement in paracetamol, L-tyrosine and 1-methyluracil evaluated against neutron benchmarks. If confirmed as described, this is evidence of hydrogen-coordinate refinement in three selected organic compounds. The supplied materials do not establish the numerical coordinate agreement, uncertainty calibration, disorder coverage or transferability to macromolecules; the review had no retained article or abstract text with which to check those details.

For neutron protein crystallography, the supplied research attributes to a 1 December 2023 Acta Crystallographica D paper by Liebschner and colleagues, DOI 10.1107/S2059798323008914, typical crystal volumes of at least 0.1 mm³ and data-collection times extending from several days to several weeks. These figures describe the practical burden reported by that source account; they should not be treated as universal lower bounds applying to every neutron experiment. Although a PDF URL is supplied, no extracted or retained text was available to the review to verify the figures or their qualifications.

The supplied account of a Crystals review dated 30 April 2024, DOI 10.3390/cryst14050433, characterizes neutron macromolecular crystallography as a specialized technique and emphasizes the severe X-ray visibility limitations of polarized hydrogen and protons, including at sub-ångström resolution. This concerns particular hydrogen and proton states and should not be expanded into a claim that X-rays never locate hydrogen. The research records a failed direct reload and an unverified author line, and the review lacked retained source text to check the characterization or its exceptions.

The supplied research describes an Acta Crystallographica D contribution dated 25 November 2025, DOI 10.1107/S2059798325009520, as a theoretical framework for dynamic-nuclear-polarization neutron measurements. On the information provided, it is a proposed route rather than evidence that routine macromolecular protonation measurements have been achieved. Its theoretical characterization and experimental status could not be checked against retained source text.

Evidence boundary: the supplied record contains dated reports of small-molecule achievements and proposals for further progress, but no captured source documents or bounded freshness search establishing the field's state as of 1 November 2026. Consequently, neither the exact reported achievements nor the continued absence of a broadly routine macromolecular method can be independently established from these inputs. Missing source access does not show that the reported results are false. The innovation remains a coherent target whose present-day degree of completion is unresolved here.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: conduct a pre-registered evaluation on at least twenty diverse ordinary-sized macromolecular or catalytic crystals, including ionizable residues and metal-containing sites. Use laboratory, standard synchrotron or electron instrumentation without requiring crystals of 0.1 mm³ or larger. The sample count and crystal-volume cutoff are proposed acceptance criteria, not established community standards. Define ordinary sample sizes, acceptable collection and processing times, radiation-dose limits and instrument requirements before testing.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed demonstration

completion_criteria.text: Proposed validation: assess hydrogen coordinates and protonation assignments separately. Compare geometry with suitable independent structural references, including neutron structures where appropriate, and assess site-specific protonation using independently informative measurements under matched chemical and physical conditions. A bulk titration can constrain overall proton uptake or acid–base behavior but may not identify individual sites and does not by itself validate hydrogen coordinates. Reference comparisons should account for differences in sample conditions rather than assuming every disagreement is a measurement error.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed validation

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reporting and reproducibility requirements: predefine site-level agreement thresholds, positional and occupancy uncertainties, treatment of competing assignments and the accounting of failed or unresolved cases. Demonstrate that independent measurements and analyses reproduce the claimed information, with enough data and methodological detail to examine model dependence. Include chemically difficult sites and disclose exclusions so that success cannot be inferred solely from the easiest hydrogens in each crystal.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed reporting and reproducibility requirements

completion_criteria.text: Proposed practical boundary: success on three well-ordered organic microcrystals would not establish the intended macromolecular and catalytic scope. A successful twenty-sample study would establish demonstrated breadth within its tested conditions, not literal universality. Claims about functional materials, strongly disordered sites or other untested regimes would require additional representative demonstrations. Completion should therefore state the validated operating range and the cases that remain unresolved.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed practical boundary

related_concepts.text: Roster-based comparison — CRX-05, Experimental many-electron quantum states of real crystals: protonation measurements and electronic-state measurements overlap because chemical bonding and electron distribution influence hydrogen observability and interpretation. CRX-09 targets hydrogen positions, occupancies and protonation assignments; full many-electron quantum-state reconstruction is not logically required for those outputs. The supplied roster gives only CRX-05's title, so its detailed technical boundary cannot be verified here.

Roster-based comparison — CRX-04, Atomic ensembles measured from total X-ray scattering, and CRX-06, Atomic movies of elementary chemical steps without a photo-trigger: ensemble information could complement CRX-09's treatment of disorder and partial occupancy, while time-resolved measurements could connect protonation changes to chemical events. Measuring a protonation state does not itself recover a complete atomic ensemble or establish the sequence and kinetics of a reaction.

Roster-based comparison — CRX-03, Chemical-accuracy prediction of which molecular crystal will form, and CRX-07, Predictive experimental selection of a chosen crystal form: measured protonation could constrain the chemical identity and interactions relevant to crystal forms, including salt-versus-cocrystal distinctions. CRX-09 supplies structural chemical information; predicting which form appears and experimentally selecting that form remain separate capabilities.

Roster-based comparison — CRX-10, Laboratory sources that do facility-class coherent X-ray crystallography; CRX-11, Diffraction-quality crystals of arbitrary macromolecules on demand; and CRX-13, A growth rulebook that suppresses defects, twins, and disorder in arbitrary crystals: improved sources and samples could make hydrogen-sensitive measurements more practical. They would not automatically resolve weak hydrogen contrast or ambiguous protonation refinement. Conversely, CRX-09 could be pursued using existing instrument classes without requiring arbitrary crystal growth or universally defect-free samples.

Roster-based comparison — CRX-12, Continuous atomic-resolution crystallography inside working devices and static extreme environments: there is overlap where protonation must be measured under operating conditions, for example in catalytic or proton-conducting materials. CRX-09 concerns chemical observability in crystals; continuous measurements inside devices or extreme environments introduce additional access, timing and environmental constraints. Demonstration under ordinary conditions would not establish those capabilities.

Roster-based comparison — CRX-01, Atomic-resolution imaging of a single non-crystalline molecule before destruction; CRX-02, Chemically complete atomic structures of bulk amorphous solids; and CRX-08, Ab initio atomic structure of matter that exists only once: all seek chemically informative atomic structure, but address different sample regimes. CRX-09's crystallographic target does not establish single-molecule imaging, bulk amorphous reconstruction or structure recovery from a unique, nonrepeatable specimen. Any transfer of hydrogen-sensitive methods to those settings would require separate evidence.

change_log.change: Preserved CRX-09's identity and expanded the target to explicitly distinguish hydrogen coordinates, occupancies and protonation assignments.
change_log.reason: The review identifies these as related but different observables, especially at disordered and partially occupied sites.

change_log.change: Replaced the claim that enzyme mechanisms and proton conduction could be read directly from structure with direct structural constraints and conditional downstream benefits.
change_log.reason: Static structures alone do not establish dynamics, reaction sequences, kinetics or transport behavior.

change_log.change: Retained the reported pharmaceutical examples, three refinement compounds, publication dates and neutron size/time figures with explicit attribution and access qualifications.
change_log.reason: The details are useful, but no retained source texts were available to verify their accuracy or scope; lack of access does not refute them.

change_log.change: Qualified broad statements about X-ray invisibility and neutron sample requirements.
change_log.reason: State-dependent hydrogen visibility and reported typical experimental requirements should not become universal claims.

change_log.change: Kept the dynamic-nuclear-polarization neutron work separate from demonstrated achievements.
change_log.reason: The supplied research describes it as theoretical, and no retained text establishes an implemented routine capability.

change_log.change: Made the proposed demonstration operational through separate coordinate and protonation validation, uncertainty thresholds, dose and throughput limits, failure accounting and reproducibility.
change_log.reason: Twenty samples alone do not establish measurement reliability, and bulk titration need not identify individual sites or hydrogen positions.

change_log.change: Separated macromolecular and catalytic validation from functional-material generalization and limited conclusions to tested operating ranges.
change_log.reason: Finite demonstrations establish breadth within tested conditions rather than universal applicability.

change_log.change: Added distinctions with every other supplied roster entry while qualifying title-based comparisons.
change_log.reason: The related concepts remain separate innovations, and their full specifications were not supplied.

unresolved_issues: The cited source documents, extracted texts and artifact hashes are absent, leaving exact findings, bibliographic identities and methodological qualifications unverified.
The supplied record does not establish whether broadly routine macromolecular protonation determination remained unavailable as of 1 November 2026; no bounded freshness search was supplied.
The numerical accuracy, occupancy sensitivity, uncertainty calibration and disorder coverage of the reported electron-diffraction refinements remain unspecified.
The scope and exceptions behind the reported neutron crystal-volume and collection-time figures require source verification.
The Crystals source's author line and detailed characterization remain unverified following the recorded failed reload.
The dynamic-nuclear-polarization contribution's characterization as theoretical, and any accompanying experimental evidence, require verification.
The proposed benchmark still needs concrete sample-size, throughput, dose, uncertainty and site-agreement thresholds, plus a defined independent replication protocol.
Suitable site-specific protonation references under matched conditions must be selected; bulk titration cannot be assumed sufficient.
Functional-material coverage needs a separately defined representative test set, and CRX-05's detailed boundary requires more than its supplied title.
